interpretations: Average of the per-group average `rental_rate` and average of the per-group film counts, over films with `rental_duration >= 5` (5 days or more counts as long), grouped by `original_language_id` with NULL as its own group, returned as one unrounded row.
Same, but with `rental_duration > 5` (strictly more than 5 days counts as long).

Same as the first, but each group is identified by the original language's name from the `language` table (joined on `original_language_id`), with films that have no original language as a separate "no language" group.
Same as the first, but groups come only from original languages that actually have at least one long-rental film, so languages with no qualifying films add no zero-count groups.

Same as the first, but every row in the `language` table is a group, so languages with no qualifying films count as groups with 0 films and a missing average. Those missing averages are ignored in the first figure, while the zero counts are included in the second.
Same as the first, but the film count per group is the number of films with a non-missing `rental_rate` (`COUNT(rental_rate)`) rather than all films in the group (`COUNT(*)`).

Same as the first, but the average of group averages is taken only over groups whose average is non-missing, and the average of group counts is taken over all groups. The first figure is NULL if no group has a non-missing average.
Same as the first, but both figures are NULL if no film meets the cutoff, since no groups remain.
Same as the first, but the two figures are returned in the order average of group film counts, then average of group average rental rates.
queries:
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) AS avg_of_avg_rental_rate, AVG(film_count) AS avg_film_count
FROM (
  SELECT original_language_id, AVG(rental_rate) AS avg_rate, COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
  GROUP BY original_language_id
);
SELECT COALESCE(l.name, 'no language') AS original_language, COUNT(*) AS films
FROM film f
LEFT JOIN language l ON l.language_id = f.original_language_id
GROUP BY COALESCE(l.name, 'no language');
SELECT l.name, COUNT(*) AS film_count
FROM film f
JOIN language l ON l.language_id = f.original_language_id
WHERE f.rental_duration >= 6
GROUP BY l.name;
SELECT AVG(avg_val), AVG(cnt)
FROM (
  SELECT l.language_id, COUNT(f.film_id) AS cnt, AVG(f.<column>) AS avg_val
  FROM language l
  LEFT JOIN film f ON f.language_id = l.language_id AND <qualifying condition>
  GROUP BY l.language_id
);
SELECT rating, COUNT(rental_rate) AS films, AVG(rental_rate), AVG(length), AVG(replacement_cost) FROM film GROUP BY rating ORDER BY films DESC;
